after_expected_public_metadata.description:
UNCERTIFIED — no hash-bound Viridis Comparator certificate covers this deposit's claims. Lean sources may compile but have not been independently certified. Results are conditional on the stated model assumptions.

Historical description:

The Intelligence Bound (IB) master inequality dI/dt <= P*D/(kB T ln 2) governs the rate at which any open thermodynamic system can accumulate Shannon information. Prior Viridis canon established five disjoint IB-saturation conditions, each pinned to a separate physical mechanism: Fisher-extremal observation channels (GIB), rank-1 Lindbladian dynamics (SSCT), Heisenberg-saturating measurement (SMT), maximal Gaian purity (KSCT), and the full mutualistic learner-environment cross-term (MELT). Whether these conditions are independent has been an open question. This paper proves the Thermodynamic Slack Decomposition Theorem (TSDT): the IB slack epsilon := P*D/(kB T ln 2) - dI/dt decomposes uniquely and additively into five non-negative, pairwise Fisher-Rao-orthogonal components -- epsilon = epsilon_geom + epsilon_rank + epsilon_meas + epsilon_decoh + epsilon_mut -- each a thermodynamic functional in closed form. The Five-Saturation Corollary characterises IB-saturating stewardship systems by the simultaneous vanishing of all five components. The paper presents three corollaries (independence, pricing, D-Score normalisation), four testable predictions, and a regulatory and financial productisation stack. TSDT is the foundational decomposition on which the symplectic-conjugation theorem of the companion paper PSIT (Planetary Symbiotic Intelligence, Run 035) is built. Part of the Viridis research canon (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19317982).
